newsitem.title: CHAD: Former Chad assembly speaker cries election foul.
newsitem.headline: Former Chad assembly speaker cries election foul.

text.p: The speaker of Chad's former transitional national assembly, Abas Ali, has accused President Idriss Deby's ruling party of using the army to intimidate voters in the January 5 parliamentary election.

But a statement from Deby's Patriotic Salvation Movement, dismissed the charge as "tendentious and without proof", noting that Abas Ali had lost his seat in the poll and should accept the verdict of the polls.
Both Abas Ali's remarks and the party statement were carried on state radio and television late on Friday.
Of 64 seats decided in the first round, Deby's party won 40. Foreign Minister Saleh Kebzabo's National Union for Development and Renewal won eight, opposition parties the rest.
The remaining 61 will go to a February 23 second round.

Abas Ali said soldiers and officials intimidated voters into supporting the ruling party in parts of the sprawling former French colony. He said his own constituency in Guera, central Chad, was one area plagued by irregularities.
Deby's party dismissed his criticism. "The first round... took place in total transparency without interference of the administration or the army," it said.

Sources close to the N'Djamena appeal court, which must vet the results, said it was still waiting for the Independent National Electoral Commission to provide affidavits to enable it to rule on complaints by certain candidates.

The elections wrap up Chad's delayed transition to democracy after decades of internal strife or war with Libya. The results confirm a political divide between Deby's Moslem north and the largely Christian south, where the opposition polled strongly.
